# dorgbr

> Generates one of the real orthogonal matrices Q or P^T determined by DGEBRD.

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import dorgbr from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/dorgbr';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
dorgbr( order, vect, M, N, K, A, LDA, TAU, strideTAU, WORK ) → integer
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `order` | `Layout` | Storage layout (`'row-major'` or `'column-major'`) |
| `vect` | `"apply-Q" \| "apply-P"` | `'apply-Q'` to generate Q, `'apply-P'` to generate P^T |
| `M` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of rows of the matrix Q or P^T<br>Requires `M ≥ 0` |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of columns of the matrix Q or P^T<br>Rejects `(N < 0 \|\| (vect === 'apply-Q' && (N > M \|\| N < min(M, K)))) \|\| (vect !== 'apply-Q' && (M > N \|\| M < min(N, K)))` |
| `K` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of columns/rows in original matrix<br>Requires `K ≥ 0` |
| `A` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>M × N</sub> | **in/out** · Input matrix |
| ↳ `LDA` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of `A`<br>Column-major requires `LDA ≥ max(1, M)`<br>Row-major requires `LDA ≥ max(1, N)` |
| `TAU` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length (vect === 'apply-P') ? min(N, K) : min(M, K)</sub> | Scalar factors of reflectors |
| ↳ `strideTAU` | `integer` | `TAU` stride length |
| `WORK` | `Float64Array \| null`<br><sub>length ≥ max(1, min(M, N))</sub> | **out** · Workspace of length at least `max(1,min(M,N))`; for optimum performance it should hold `min(M,N)*NB` elements (`NB = 32`), which enables the blocked path; if `null`, a workspace of the optimal size is allocated |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `vect`: Specifies whether the matrix Q or the matrix $P^T$ is required, as defined in the transformation applied by DGEBRD:

  -   `= 'Q'`: generate Q;
  -   `= 'P'`: generate $P^T$.
- `M`: The number of rows of the matrix Q or $P^T$ to be returned. $M \ge 0$.
- `N`: The number of columns of the matrix Q or $P^T$ to be returned. $N \ge 0$. If `VECT = 'Q'`, $M \ge N \ge \min (M,K)$; if `VECT = 'P'`, $N \ge M \ge \min (N,K)$.
- `K`: If `VECT = 'Q'`, the number of columns in the original M-by-K matrix reduced by DGEBRD. If `VECT = 'P'`, the number of rows in the original K-by-N matrix reduced by DGEBRD. $K \ge 0$.
- `A`: On entry, the vectors which define the elementary reflectors, as returned by DGEBRD. On exit, the M-by-N matrix Q or $P^T$.
- `TAU`: (min(N,K)) if `VECT = 'P'` `TAU(i)` must contain the scalar factor of the elementary reflector H(i) or G(i), which determines Q or $P^T$, as returned by DGEBRD in its array argument TAUQ or TAUP.
- `WORK`: On exit, if `INFO = 0`, `WORK(1)` returns the optimal `LWORK`.

</details>

**Returns** `integer`: info status code

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be a valid order
- `TypeError` second argument must be one of the following: "apply-P", "apply-Q"
- `RangeError` third argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` fourth argument is invalid (rejected when `( N < 0 \|\| ( vect === "apply-Q" && ( N > M \|\| N < min( M, K ) ) ) ) \|\| ( vect !== "apply-Q" && ( M > N \|\| M < min( N, K ) ) )`)
- `RangeError` fifth argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` seventh argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, M )` (column-major)
- `RangeError` seventh argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, N )` (row-major)

### Strided (ndarray) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
dorgbr.ndarray(
    vect,
    M, N, K,
    A, strideA1, strideA2, offsetA,
    TAU, strideTAU, offsetTAU,
    WORK, strideWork, offsetWork
) → integer
```

Generates one of the real orthogonal matrices Q or P^T determined by DGEBRD when reducing a real matrix to bidiagonal form `A = Q*B*P^T`.

Matrix shapes are logical (rows × columns). The reference's leading dimension (`LDA`, …) is replaced by the two strides and the offset.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `vect` | `"apply-Q" \| "apply-P"` | `'apply-Q'` to generate Q, `'apply-P'` to generate P^T |
| `M` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of rows of the matrix Q or P^T<br>Requires `M ≥ 0` |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of columns of the matrix Q or P^T<br>Rejects `(N < 0 \|\| (vect === 'apply-Q' && (N > M \|\| N < min(M, K)))) \|\| (vect !== 'apply-Q' && (M > N \|\| M < min(N, K)))` |
| `K` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of columns/rows in original matrix<br>Requires `K ≥ 0` |
| `A` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>M × N</sub> | **in/out** · Matrix containing reflectors from DGEBRD |
| ↳ `strideA1` | `integer` | Stride of the first dimension of A |
| ↳ `strideA2` | `integer` | Stride of the second dimension of A |
| ↳ `offsetA` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for A |
| `TAU` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length (vect === 'apply-P') ? min(N, K) : min(M, K)</sub> | Scalar factors of reflectors |
| ↳ `strideTAU` | `integer` | Stride for TAU |
| ↳ `offsetTAU` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for TAU |
| `WORK` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length ≥ max(1, min(M, N))</sub> | **out** · Workspace of length at least `max(1,min(M,N))`; for optimum performance it should hold `min(M,N)*NB` elements (`NB = 32`, the dorgqr/dorglq block size), which enables the blocked path |
| ↳ `strideWork` | `integer` | Stride for WORK (must be 1) |
| ↳ `offsetWork` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for WORK |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `vect`: Specifies whether the matrix Q or the matrix $P^T$ is required, as defined in the transformation applied by DGEBRD:

  -   `= 'Q'`: generate Q;
  -   `= 'P'`: generate $P^T$.
- `M`: The number of rows of the matrix Q or $P^T$ to be returned. $M \ge 0$.
- `N`: The number of columns of the matrix Q or $P^T$ to be returned. $N \ge 0$. If `VECT = 'Q'`, $M \ge N \ge \min (M,K)$; if `VECT = 'P'`, $N \ge M \ge \min (N,K)$.
- `K`: If `VECT = 'Q'`, the number of columns in the original M-by-K matrix reduced by DGEBRD. If `VECT = 'P'`, the number of rows in the original K-by-N matrix reduced by DGEBRD. $K \ge 0$.
- `A`: On entry, the vectors which define the elementary reflectors, as returned by DGEBRD. On exit, the M-by-N matrix Q or $P^T$.
- `TAU`: (min(N,K)) if `VECT = 'P'` `TAU(i)` must contain the scalar factor of the elementary reflector H(i) or G(i), which determines Q or $P^T$, as returned by DGEBRD in its array argument TAUQ or TAUP.
- `WORK`: On exit, if `INFO = 0`, `WORK(1)` returns the optimal `LWORK`.

</details>

**Returns** `integer`: info status code (0 if successful)

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be one of the following: "apply-P", "apply-Q"
- `RangeError` second argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` third argument is invalid (rejected when `( N < 0 \|\| ( vect === "apply-Q" && ( N > M \|\| N < min( M, K ) ) ) ) \|\| ( vect !== "apply-Q" && ( M > N \|\| M < min( N, K ) ) )`)
- `RangeError` fourth argument must be a nonnegative integer

### Status codes

An `info` status code: `0` on success. A positive value reports a numerical condition such as a singular pivot or a failure to converge (see the description). Invalid arguments throw instead of returning a negative `info`. Returns immediately when `M === 0 || N === 0`.

The reference documents `INFO` as:

-   `= 0`: successful exit
-   `< 0`: if `INFO = -i`, the i-th argument had an illegal value

</section>

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import discreteUniform from '@stdlib/random/array/discrete-uniform/lib/index.js';
import dorgbr from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/dorgbr';

/** @type {{ dtype: 'float64' }} */
const opts = {
	'dtype': 'float64'
};
const N = 3;
const A = discreteUniform( N * N, -10, 10, opts );
const TAU = discreteUniform( N, -10, 10, opts );
const WORK = discreteUniform( N, -10, 10, opts );

// Using the standard interface:
let out = dorgbr( 'row-major', 'apply-Q', N, N, N, A, N, TAU, 1, WORK );
console.log( out );

// Using the ndarray interface:
out = dorgbr.ndarray( 'apply-Q', N, N, N, A, N, 1, 0, TAU, 1, 0, WORK, 1, 0 );
console.log( out );
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference LAPACK 3.12.0 source of `DORGBR`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

DORGBR generates one of the real orthogonal matrices Q or $P^T$ determined by DGEBRD when reducing a real matrix A to bidiagonal form: $A = Q \, B \, P^T$. Q and $P^T$ are defined as products of elementary reflectors H(i) or G(i) respectively.

If `VECT = 'Q'`, A is assumed to have been an M-by-K matrix, and Q is of order M: if $m \ge k$, $Q = H(1)$ H(2) . . . H(k) and DORGBR returns the first n columns of Q, where $m \ge n \ge k$; if $m < k$, $Q = H(1)$ H(2) . . . H(m-1) and DORGBR returns Q as an M-by-M matrix.

If `VECT = 'P'`, A is assumed to have been a K-by-N matrix, and $P^T$ is of order N: if $k < n$, $P^T = G(k)$ . . . G(2) G(1) and DORGBR returns the first m rows of $P^T$, where $n \ge m \ge k$; if $k \ge n$, $P^T = G(n-1)$ . . . G(2) G(1) and DORGBR returns $P^T$ as an N-by-N matrix.

</section>
